title: Ghee Rice (Nei Choru)
tagline: Rich, aromatic basmati cooked in ghee with whole spices and fried onions.
intro: Ghee rice — nei choru in Kerala and ghee bath elsewhere — is understated luxury: basmati cooked in fragrant ghee with whole spices and crowned with fried onions and cashews. Mild, buttery and festive, it's a favourite for weddings in the South and a wonderful backdrop for rich curries.

items: 400 g (2 cups) basmati rice, soaked 20 min
1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 bay leaf, 1 star anise
700 ml hot water or light stock

method: Fry the sliced onions in ghee until golden; set aside half for garnish.
To the remaining onions add fennel and the whole spices; let them sizzle.
Add ginger–garlic paste, then the drained rice, and stir gently in the ghee for a minute.
Add the hot water and salt. Boil, cover and cook on low until absorbed, 12–15 minutes.
Fry the cashews and raisins in the extra ghee until golden.
Fluff the rice and top with the fried onions, cashews and raisins.
tips: Using hot water keeps the grains from breaking.
Don't skimp on the ghee — it's the point of the dish.
toServe: Traditionally served with a rich meat or vegetable korma.
imageAlt: Ghee rice topped with fried onions, cashews and raisins
